artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan cutting shell-suite wall time via a verify-deploy.sh --only-gate flag (~290s of ~650s) plus opt-in run-all.sh file-level parallelism behind a 3-run flakiness decision gate, with a measured before/after baseline and a per-suite coverage-equality proof.

memory_candidates.content: Performance planning for a test suite must start from a full-suite measurement, not from a plausible structural story. In the agent-system shell suite the named suspect (process-spawn amplification: 46 subprocess re-execs in one file, 'each re-sources 5+ libraries and re-parses state.json') measured at 0.8% of total wall time, while an unnamed file was 60% of it -- because it invoked the real verify-deploy.sh four times to test ONE of its 20 gates, and verify-deploy.sh had no gate-selection flag. Micro-measurements: sourcing a shared shell lib costs ~0.1ms over bare `bash -c ':'`; a jq read of a 1200-line JSON state file ~5ms. Generalizable pattern: when a test is slow because it exercises one unit of a monolithic production script, the highest-value fix is usually an additive selection flag in the PRODUCTION script (keeping one full-battery invocation somewhere for the all-units-together contract), not test-side fixture reuse or parallelism. Order the work: measure, then gate-select, then parallelize, then micro-optimize.
